passages.P3: # We are the investigative journalists who worked on the Panama Papers AMA!
passages.P6: over a year ago, an anonymous source contacted the *Süddeutsche Zeitung* (SZ) and submitted encrypted internal documents from Mossack Fonseca, a Panamanian law firm that sells anonymous offshore companies around the world.
passages.P7: Ultimately, SZ acquired about 2.6 terabytes of data, making the leak the biggest that journalists had ever worked with. The source wanted neither financial compensation nor anything else in return, apart from a few security measures. The *Süddeutsche Zeitung* decided to analyze the data in cooperation with the *International Consortium of Investigative Journalists* (ICIJ). In the past 12 months, around 400 journalists from more than 100 media organizations in over 80 countries have taken part in researching the documents.
passages.P8: We are three of them, and very happy to finally be able to talk about the work we did in the last year!
passages.P9: **For further information on the Panama Papers:** **http://panamapapers.sueddeutsche.de/en**
passages.P11:
* Frederik Obermaier, Investigative Reporter, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Twitter: @f\_obermaier
* Bastian Obermayer, Investigative Reporter, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Twitter: @b\_obermayer
* Vanessa Wormer, Data Journalist, Süddeutsche Zeitung, Twitter: @Remrow
passages.P12: If you have information for us, please contact us at **investigativ[at]sz.de** or via our **PGP Key**: http://pgp.mit.edu/pks/lookup?op=get&search=0xE98F78D8CC45D096
passages.P13: **One small favor before we start:** Due to legal matters and in order to protect our source, we might not be able to answer all of your questions. But we’ll try our best to give you a look behind the scenes and tell you how we worked on the Panama Papers.
passages.P14: **EDIT: Frederik has to leave now but Bastian and Vanessa are still here to answer your questions!**
passages.P15: **EDIT 2: That was awesome! Now we have to go and eat pizza. Thank you for all these amazing questions, that was a lot of fun! We are going to check this subreddit again tomorrow, if we oversaw any major aspect we are going to figure out a way to reply on it later.**
passages.P16: Archived post. New comments cannot be posted and votes cannot be cast.
passages.P19: The action never stops. Catch new episodes of Alaska State Troopers, Ozark Law, and Southern Law Wednesdays starting at 8pm ET, only on A&E.
passages.P27: I have a few questions for you:
passages.P28:
1. Does anyone else besides yourselves have a full copy of that data (eg the other 100 media organisations/400 journalists?), if so how would you stop one of them leaking the data to the world?
2. I had wondered about the legitimacy of that data. Obviously some of it must be good otherwise we wouldn't have seen people resign over the leaks etc. How can you verify the authenticity of each article/document? How would we know if one of the stories that came out was fabricated or incorrect?
3. Finally, how did you agree who was getting which stories or have you split the data up between everyone? If so how did that work? Did some media outlets think they should get more or better stories etc?
passages.P34: Can you speak a little about your technology and how you are actually parsing through 2.6TB of data?

passages.P1: ## Missouri Voters Just Made It Much Harder for Lawmakers to Overturn Citizen-Led Initiatives
passages.P2: For years, Missouri Republicans worked to undo or restrict voter-approved laws and amendments. In passing Amendment 6, voters have not only protected the ballot initiative process but also dramatically strengthened their power over the legislature.
passages.P3: ## Trump’s State Department Is Giving $1 Million to Controversial Group to Study Crimes Against White South Africans
passages.P4: The new award, the administration’s latest show of support for the Afrikaner cause, comes after it cut human rights funding to nations in crisis. One former diplomat called the move “offensive.”
passages.P5: ## SafeSport Will Now Alert Schools, Clubs if Coaches Sanctioned for Abuse Continue to Work With Kids
passages.P6: The U.S. Center for SafeSport is taking new steps to protect children from athletic coaches banned over abuse allegations. The move follows a ProPublica-Washington Post investigation that found several sanctioned coaches continued to work with kids.
passages.P7: ## Vermont Has Spent Nearly a Billion Dollars to Clean Up Lake Champlain. But the Green Slime Keeps Coming Back.
passages.P8: Vermont kicked off an ambitious effort in 2015 to clean up waterways and meet tougher EPA restrictions. But after a decade and nearly a billion dollars spent, potentially toxic algae still lingers in Lake Champlain. What happened?
passages.P9: Vermont Was Supposed to Get an Audit of Its Lake Champlain Cleanup. It Never Happened.
passages.P10: Do You Live Near Lake Champlain? Help Seven Days and ProPublica Investigate Algae Blooms.
passages.P11: ## I Was There to Document the Aftermath of Deadly Flooding. Then, It Started Raining.
passages.P12: Three people died in Ruidoso, New Mexico, last year when floods swept through the area. As the mayor prioritized tourism after the flood recovery, first responders said they weren’t equipped. Our visual journalist documented the unfolding story.
passages.P13: Town Leaders Said They Were Prepared for Floods. First Responders Disagree.
passages.P14: ## Inside Trump’s Futile Hunt for Noncitizen Voters
passages.P15: Claiming that hundreds of thousands of noncitizens were voting illegally, Trump tasked agents who usually investigate cross-border crime with uncovering proof. We followed along to find out: How many of these voters could there actually be?
passages.P16: ProPublica is a nonprofit, investigative newsroom that exposes corruption. We report in all 50 states and partner with local newsrooms. Our work spurs real-world impact and has received numerous awards, including nine Pulitzer Prizes. Read more
passages.P20: The Ugly Truth Behind MLB’s Recruiting Paradise
passages.P21: In a country where baseball is king, a corrosive system preys on young players’ dreams of major league stardom and financial security.
passages.P23: Teams make handshake deals with players as young as 11 while moneylenders prey on their families. The industry is corrupt, but Major League Baseball and the players union have done little about it.
passages.P24: ### The Rising Baseball Star, a Fatal Car Crash and the Fixer
passages.P25: When an accident involving top prospect Oneil Cruz left three dead on a darkened road in the Dominican Republic, secret payoffs helped rescue his career and launched a shadowy business empire.
passages.P27: ### Making America Healthy? Examining the Raw Claims and Real Risks of MAHA.
passages.P28: Join us for a special conversation with ProPublica reporters investigating the “Make America Healthy Again” movement and how it is putting children at risk.
